cues: A system is separated from its surroundings by a boundary.
Work done by a gas is the area under its P V curve.
The first law says Q equals delta U plus W, and for an ideal gas U depends only on temperature.
Each of the four processes turns the first law into one simple line.
In a cycle, delta U is zero and the work is the loop area.
C p minus C v equals R. Isothermal work is n R T ln V two over V one, and in an adiabatic change P V to the gamma stays constant.
text: Let us recap. A system is separated from its surroundings by a boundary. Work done by a gas is the area under its P V curve. The first law says Q equals delta U plus W, and for an ideal gas U depends only on temperature. Each of the four processes turns the first law into one simple line. In a cycle, delta U is zero and the work is the loop area. C p minus C v equals R. Isothermal work is n R T ln V two over V one, and in an adiabatic change P V to the gamma stays constant.
